AccountType.description: The class of an account; it decides its normal balance and the statement it reports on.

ApprovalReason.description: Why a quotation or an order needs approval before it is issued or confirmed.

BankReconciliationStatus.description: Where a bank reconciliation is in its life.

BarcodeType.description: What kind of code a barcode is; EAN-13 and GTIN values follow GS1 and carry a check digit.

CashAccountKind.description: Whether a treasury account is a cashbox or a bank account.

CatalogDataIssue.description: A gap or inconsistency in a product's master data, found by the catalog data-quality report.

CatalogImportAction.description: What confirming an import will do with one row.

CatalogImportMode.description:
What a catalog import does with a row whose code (unit or category code, SKU, product unit, barcode) already exists.
New rows are always created. An import never deletes, deactivates or reactivates anything.

CatalogImportSheet.description: The kinds of rows a catalog import holds, in the order they are applied.

CreditHoldPolicy.description: What a customer's manual credit hold does to a new order.

CustomerAddressType.description: What a customer's address is used for.

CustomerType.description: Who the customer is; fixed once created.

FiscalPeriodStatus.description: Whether journals may still post into a period.

FiscalYearAction.description: One step in a fiscal year's history.

FiscalYearStatus.description: Whether a fiscal year has been closed into retained earnings.

JournalAction.description: One step in a journal's history.

JournalStatus.description: Where a journal is in its life. Only posted journals count in balances, and a posted journal never changes.

JournalType.description: Where a journal comes from; each type has its own number series per fiscal year.

LocationImportAction.description: What confirming a location import will do with one row.

LocationImportMode.description:
What a location import does with a row whose location (branch, warehouse and location code) already exists. New
rows are always created. An import never moves a location, never changes a code, never activates or deactivates.

OrganizationDataIssue.description:
A configuration problem the master-data quality report finds. Only states the database and the domain rules still
allow are reported; what they already make impossible (a selling transit warehouse, two default locations) is not.

OrganizationEntity.description: The kind of record a master-data quality issue is about.

PosCardIncidentStatus.description: Where a card incident (a card approved for a checkout POS could not record) stands.

PosCashMovementType.description: Cash put into or taken out of a shift's drawer outside sales and refunds.

PosPaymentMethod.description: How a POS sale is paid or a return refunded.

PosPaymentStatus.description: What POS knows about a payment or a refund it recorded.

PosReturnCondition.description: The state goods come back in. V1 takes back only goods fit for resale; anything else is refused.

PosShiftAction.description: One step in a shift's history.

PosShiftStatus.description: Where a cashier shift is in its life.

PostingRole.description:
What an account is used for when the system writes a journal by itself (year-end close now; ERP postings later). Each
role is mapped explicitly to one posting account; nothing in the code names an account, and an unmapped role stops
the posting that needs it instead of falling back to a default.

PriceSource.description: Where a line's unit price came from; the price is a snapshot either way.

ProductType.description: Whether a product is held in stock.

PurchaseOrderStatus.description: Where a purchase order is in its life.

PurchaseRequestStatus.description: Where a purchase request is in its life.

PurchasingDocumentAction.description: A step in a purchasing document's history.

PurchasingDocumentType.description: A kind of purchasing document; each has its own number series per branch and fiscal year.

ReturnCondition.description:
The state returned goods arrive in. Only goods confirmed fit for resale go back into sellable stock in V1; the other
conditions are refused explicitly (Inventory has no quarantine or non-sellable stock yet), never restocked.

SalesDeliveryStatus.description: Where a delivery note is in its life.

SalesDocumentAction.description: A step in a sales document's history.

SalesDocumentType.description: A kind of sales document; each has its own number series per branch and fiscal year.

SalesInvoiceStatus.description: Where a sales invoice is in its life.

SalesOrderStatus.description: Where a sales order is in its life.

SalesQuotationStatus.description: Where a quotation is in its life. An issued quotation past its validity date shows as expired.

SalesReturnStatus.description: Where a customer return is in its life.

SalesTaxTreatment.description: How VAT applies to a sales line. Anything else is refused, never treated as one of these.

SourcePostingStatus.description: Where the journal of an operational document stands.

StockCountAction.description: A step in a stock count's history.

StockCountStatus.description: Where a stock count is in its life.

StockDocumentAction.description: A step in a stock document's history.

StockDocumentStatus.description: Where a stock document is in its life.

StockDocumentType.description: What a stock document does; each type has its own number series.

StockStatus.description: The condition stock is in; only available stock counts as sellable.

StockTransferAction.description: A step in a transfer's history.

StockTransferStatus.description: Where a transfer is in its life.

SupplierAddressType.description: What a supplier's address is used for.

SupplierInvoiceStatus.description: Where a supplier invoice is in its life.

SupplierReturnStatus.description: Where a supplier return is in its life.

TaxTreatment.description: How a line's tax is treated in cost.

TrackingMode.description: How individual units of a stock item are told apart.
